prompt:
A scientific probe of mass 140 kg falls vertically through an atmosphere. At a certain instant, the downward acceleration of the probe is 3.50 m s^-2. The acceleration of free fall is 9.81 m s^-2.
(a) Calculate the resultant downward force acting on the probe at this instant. [1]
(b) Calculate the drag force acting on the probe at this instant. [2]
hints: Set up F_net = mg - D to find drag force D in part (b).
solution:
(a) Resultant force F_net = ma = 140 kg x 3.50 m s^-2 = 490 N.
(b) Weight W = mg = 140 kg x 9.81 m s^-2 = 1373.4 N.
Resultant force F_net = W - D => D = W - F_net = 1373.4 N - 490 N = 883 N.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: In part (a), apply Newton's second law directly: F_net = 140 x 3.50 = 490 N.
Step 2: In part (b), calculate downward weight: W = 140 x 9.81 = 1373.4 N.
Step 3: Relate forces: F_net = W - D, so D = W - F_net = 1373.4 - 490 = 883.4 N.
Step 4: Round to 3 significant figures: 883 N.

mark_scheme.criterion: Calculates W = mg = 140 x 9.81 = 1373 N and sets D = W - F_net
